title:
Space engineering
Adoption Notice of CCSDS 232.1-B-2, Communications Operation Procedure-1
organisation: ECSS Secretariat, ESA-ESTEC Requirements & Standards Division (prepared by the ECSS Space Communications Working Group)
status_notes: First issue of 1 March 2021; together with ECSS-E-AS-50-24C and ECSS-E-AS-50-25C it replaces ECSS-E-ST-50-04C (change log, p. 3). The scope notes that a later CCSDS technical corrigendum to 232.1-B-2 does not affect this notice (p. 5). The library's ECSS-E-AS-50-25C Rev.1 (13 January 2023) still lists ECSS-E-AS-50-26C without a revision in its bibliography.
summary:
A short ECSS **Adoption Notice** that makes the CCSDS Blue Book **CCSDS 232.1-B-2, Communications Operation Procedure-1 (Issue 2, September 2010)** applicable to ECSS projects with one targeted modification. COP-1 is the retransmission protocol used with the TC Space Data Link Protocol. The sending end (FOP-1) and the receiving end (FARM-1) cooperate, through the CLCW report, to deliver telecommand frames in order, without gaps or duplicates. COP-1 was previously specified in clause 7 of ECSS-E-ST-50-04C, which this notice supersedes jointly with ECSS-E-AS-50-24C (TC coding) and ECSS-E-AS-50-25C (TC data link). Page 6 tabulates each superseded ECSS-E-ST-50-0x standard against its adoption notice and the CCSDS issue it was based on in 2021.

The single normative change (Table 4-1, clause 3.3.2) concerns **Type-BD (bypass) frames** arriving when no FARM-1 back-end buffer is free. CCSDS lets the buffer contents be erased and an *optional* 'Aborted Indication' be sent. ECSS instead makes this explicit: the **FDU Arrived Indication** gains a parameter, the **FDU aborted indication**. It is set only when a Type-BD frame was accepted with no buffer available, which tells the higher procedures that buffered data was overwritten.

Informative Annex A records the one other difference from ECSS-E-ST-50-04C: that standard had special requirements for a FARM-1 with a single back-end buffer per virtual channel, which CCSDS 232.1-B-2 does not include. The bibliography lists the full family of ECSS-E-AS-50-2x notices, the superseded 2008 standards and the CCSDS TC coding Green Book.

key_points.text: CCSDS 232.1-B-2, Communications Operation Procedure-1, Issue 2, September 2010 applies with the modifications in Table 4-1.
A recently published technical corrigendum to CCSDS 232.1-B-2 does not affect the Adoption Notice.
COP-1 is used with the TC Space Data Link Protocol to deliver frames in sequence and without gaps or duplication; it was previously clause 7 of ECSS-E-ST-50-04.
In 2021 the adoption notices were based on CCSDS 131.0-B-3 (Sept. 2017), 132.0-B-2 (Sept. 2015), 732.0-B-3 (August 2016), 231.0-B-3 (Sept. 2017), 232.0-B-3 (Sept. 2015) and 232.1-B-2 (Sept. 2010).

Clause 3.3.2 is modified: when a Type-BD frame is accepted by FARM-1 with no buffer available, the buffer data is erased and the FDU Arrived Indication carries a new 'FDU aborted indication' parameter (GVCID, FDU aborted indication).
The FDU aborted indication is set only when a Type-BD Transfer Frame is accepted by FARM-1 and there is no buffer available; the optional CCSDS 'Aborted Indication' signal is removed.
ECSS-E-ST-50-04 had requirements for a FARM-1 with only one back-end buffer per virtual channel; this special case is not in CCSDS 232.1-B-2.

notes: There is no normative-references clause. CCSDS 232.1-B-2 is listed as 'normative' because clause 4a makes it applicable (p. 8). The context clause names the superseded companion as 'ECSS-E-ST-50-24C' (p. 6), where ECSS-E-AS-50-24C is meant, and Annex A.1 refers to itself as 'AS ECSS-E-AS-50-232.1-B-2' (p. 11). The context clause says differences are described 'in the informative Annex A', but the table of contents (p. 4) does not list Annex A or the Bibliography (they are on pp. 11-12). The title page says 'Requirements & Standards Division', while ECSS-E-AS-50-25C Rev.1 says 'Section'. The extraction of Table 4-1 interleaves columns (p. 9). Printed page numbers equal PDF page numbers, and PDF page 13 is blank.
